nodes.label: desktop memory - how the tagging stage is validated during the build

Frozen copy taken 2026-08-03 of the desktop machine's memory file - the live directory sits on the other machine and is not reachable from here, so this copy is what there is to review. Listed unreviewed in REVIEW_REGISTER.md section 6. Resolved 2026-06-08: how the expensive tagging stage is validated DURING the build so a small error surfaces on the first chunks rather than after the whole corpus is tagged - the dichotomy 'bulletproof everything versus run blind' is FALSE. Two materials: the deterministic prefix - probe, reference, structure, chunk - is pure functions over sacred source, so it runs on the whole corpus free with no LLM, dumping artifacts and golden-tested, robust because running is free; while the tagger is the ONLY expensive and stochastic part, its quality an empirical unknown, validated only by running and looking, so a sample run IS the method rather than a compromise. The expensive call's outputs each get their cheapest test, with the description arm removed 2026-06-11 because the description is dead and the tagger emits phrase tags only, no numbers: tags get data-quality assertions in code with no LLM, instant at N=1 - MUST-NOT rules barring employee-ids, dates and PR-numbers as concepts, and closed-vocabulary membership where a closed set applies; weights, measured and never model-emitted, get no isolated unit test for correctness, only cheap invariant assertions that weights must discriminate, with real validation end-to-end via gold-100 retrieval. Error-analysis-by-reading PRECEDES the assertions: run the real tagger on 20-40 chunks across content-kinds, read each output against its source, journal into a failure taxonomy, then count - the assertions are discovered by looking, not specified up front. Sample size, catching versus measuring: about 30 draws catches a frequent bug by the binomial, while measuring a rate with a tight interval needs 250-500
